title: Legacy webhook-bridge termination and client migration playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: We currently support a legacy webhook callback compatibility layer (the "webhook-bridge") that translates old-style callback registrations and payloads into our newer eventing and streaming model. The bridge increases operational burden, carries historical security risks (unsigned payloads, permissive retry semantics), and prevents us from consolidating telemetry and billing on the v2 event API. Goal: safely retire the webhook-bridge and require clients to adopt one of two supported integrations: (1) direct Webhook v2 (signed payloads, schema v2) for async callbacks or (2) Unified Streaming/Server-Sent Events (SSE) for low-latency responses. This ticket is the product playbook for timelines, migration requirements, SDK and documentation deliverables, telemetry gates and acceptance criteria. Scope: public hosted API webhook-bridge endpoints, corresponding Console UI for callback registration, and published SDK adapters. Not in scope: on-prem/private deployments (those will be handled under a separate private-deployment plan).
migration_guidance_summary: We will publish a migration guide and two tooling options: (A) a lightweight adapter library in Node/Python that translates webhook-bridge semantics to Webhook v2; (B) a CLI migration helper that validates customer payload schemas and simulates v2 signing. Recommend: low-latency applications move to Streaming/SSE; async background jobs move to Webhook v2. Provide example recipes, test harness, and preflight checks in Console for customers to validate endpoints before cutover.
acceptance_criteria: Public migration guide published and linked from Console documentation
Node and Python adapter libraries released (semver minor) with automated tests and sample apps
Migration CLI (validate + signed-test) available and documented
Top 20 customers by webhook usage invited to pilot and at least 10 complete migration successfully during pilot
Operational metrics show <1% increase in 5xx for migrated customers and <0.5% total increase platform-wide during staged cutover
Telemetry shows at least 75% of active webhook registrations migrated or replaced within 90-day migration window
Console UI updated to prevent new registrations on webhook-bridge and to surface migration status per token/route
Security review and KMS/signing requirements completed and documented
Rollback runbook defined and tested in staging (simulated rollback within 30 minutes)
rollout_plan: Week 0 — Announcement: publish deprecation FAQ, timeline, and high-level migration options; email affected customers; post Console banner
Week 1-4 — SDK & tooling: publish Node/Python adapters and migration CLI; design migrate-by-default Console workflow
Week 5-8 — Pilot: onboard top webhook customers (invite-only) and run migration assistance with Solutions Eng; iterate on docs
Week 9-12 — Gradual region-by-region cutover: disable new webhook-bridge registrations; enable Console preflight checks and telemetry gating
Day 90 — Soft cutover: stop deliveries for non-migrated webhook-bridge endpoints but keep a read-only compatibility log for 30 days
Day 120 — Final cutover: retire bridge completely and remove support; archive compatibility logs and update billing/metrics
telemetry_gates: Gate A (pilot completion): pilot cohort average success rate >= 90% for end-to-end validation tests
Gate B (pre-cutover): platform error rate for calls routed to webhook flows < 2% for 72h sustained
Gate C (cutover readiness): at least 65% of active webhook registrations either migrated, scheduled, or flagged for manual support
Abort condition: if platform-wide 5xx increases > 3% for more than 2 consecutive days, pause cutover and open incident review
owner_notes: We should avoid the phrase "sunset" in customer comms; use "retirement of legacy bridge" and focus on security & performance benefits
Coordinate PRD and legal on data retention for archived compatibility logs (30 days max unless customer requests extension)
Plan Solutions Eng field time for the first 6 weeks of pilot and offer a migration credit for heavy users to reduce churn risk
